mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained federal funds rate increase above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand, driving corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month averages, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 5.0%), accelerating labor market growth (PAYEMS > 3-month average) signals sustained economic momentum, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods (UNRATE < 5.0%) with PAYEMS growth, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) indicates economic contraction, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO < 100.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market conditions (PAYEMS growth above 3-month average) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS growth and UNRATE < 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) consistently signal strong residential construction and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of the absolute level.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with HOUST above 1000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates economic weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
